ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.08572v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: This research involved the study of an application of Case-Based Reasoning (CBR) in the field of academic advising. Academic advisement has been recognised as an important function of higher education. However, there is a widespread desire to improve the advisement services provided by many educational institutions (e.g., colleges and universities) around the world. ArXiv cs.AI.title: NormGym: Evaluating Normative Competence through Social Interaction
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.08613v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Normative competence, the ability to infer socially enforced expectations from interaction and adjust behavior accordingly, is essential for agents operating in unfamiliar human communities. Yet existing evaluations largely test whether agents can recognize or apply norms they may already know, rather than whether they can acquire previously unknown norms from social interaction. We introduce NormGym, an interactive benchmark for normative competence in which a newcomer must infer a hidden, arbitrary norm while pursuing its own task in a multi-a

ArXiv cs.AI.title: LLM-Based Feature Extraction for Multi-Criteria Inventory Classification
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.08626v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: E-commerce supply chains generate large volumes of customer feedback and operational data that remain underutilized in inventory management. Traditional inventory classification techniques such as ABC analysis rely primarily on annual dollar usage, while multi-criteria inventory classification (MCIC) methods extend this but still depend on structured quantitative data and do not utilize unstructured information available in modern supply chains. This paper proposes an LLM-based feature extraction approach that transforms unstructured sources suc

ArXiv cs.AI.title: Aspect-wise Pairwise Tournaments for Test-Time Selection
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.08640v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Scaling test-time compute has proven highly effective at improving LLM reasoning. A popular method is best-of-n sampling, where a model generates many candidate solutions and one is selected. This motivates the question: how can we select the best candidate? When humans make choices, we find it more natural to compare two options than judge each in isolation. ArXiv cs.AI.title: Decision Context: Persistent Behavioral Learning for AI Agents
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.08644v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: LLM agents do not learn from corrections across sessions. A user fixes the same mistake at the start of every conversation. Existing agent memory systems primarily handle facts, such as preferences, entities, and conversational history, rather than procedural knowledge.
  We present Forge Decision Context (forge_dc), a system that captures behavioral signals from human corrections and self-assessed tool-call failures, compiles them into imperative RULE directives, and injects them at the decision points where they apply. We evaluate forge_dc alo

ArXiv cs.AI.title: IWIBench: Evaluating Gradient-Free Model Driven Intra-weight Injection
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.08647v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Intra-weight injection lets one model change another model's behaviour by editing its weights directly, without gradients. Such edits can range from altering lexical associations to enforcing output formats or updating factual knowledge. Despite growing interest in these approaches, there has been no systematic way to evaluate how well models perform them. ArXiv cs.AI.title: Pdb or Not to Be: Comparing Debugging Interfaces With Pass$_{X}$@$k$
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.08666v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Interactive debuggers are indispensable to human software development, yet coding agents overwhelmingly rely on edit-execute-observe loops, using common bash tools, test scripts, and print statements to debug via repeated shell commands. Stepping through a debugger provides live access to runtime state, which may enable different problem-solving capabilities. However, prior work typically introduces the debugger as an additional tool or through a new subagent, making its individual contribution difficult to isolate from the associated scaffold c

ArXiv cs.AI.title: ChainFlow: Few-Step Latent Flow Matching for Speculative Decoding
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.08669v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Speculative decoding has become a standard way to accelerate LLM inference: a lightweight drafter proposes tokens that the target verifies in one parallel pass. Existing drafters face trade-offs that limits their speedups: autoregressive drafters generate tokens one at a time, so drafting cost grows with draft length, while diffusion drafters generate tokens in parallel but predict each position independently, ignoring inter-token dependencies. ArXiv cs.AI.title: Transporting the Past: An Optimal Transport View of Backtracking Counterfactuals
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.08682v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study backtracking counterfactual inference for Structural Causal Models (SCMs) through the lens of optimal transport. In SCMs, a factual observation generally induces a posterior distribution over exogenous variables, making counterfactual inference inherently distributional. We introduce two complementary frameworks that transport this posterior onto the set of exogenous configurations satisfying a desired counterfactual query. ArXiv cs.AI.title: Cancellation Is Not Enough: What Retries Leave Behind in an Overloaded LLM Engine
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.08684v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Clients and proxies in front of an LLM engine retry calls that time out. After a transient overload, these retries can keep the engine from recovering even when calls arrive below its capacity. Since the engine may keep computing for clients that have left, propagating cancellation looks like the natural remedy. In this paper, we test it on vLLM with overload experiments on three open models, and with scheduler traces of one that follow each client attempt to the execution it creates in the engine. ArXiv cs.AI.title: Memory-Aware Multi-Agent Architecture with LLM-based Orchestration for Conversational Recommendation
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.08718v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Conversational recommender systems often treat user sessions in isolation, limiting their ability to capture how user intent evolves over time. While large language models (LLMs) have improved semantic understanding, they are typically used as isolated components, without addressing how memory, retrieval, and decision-making should be integrated at the system level. In this work, we propose a memory-aware multi-agent architecture for conversational recommendation, in which LLMs act as orchestration layers that coordinate intent refinement, query

ArXiv cs.AI.title: AlterNet: Adaptive-Depth Mixture-of-Experts with Learned Halting for Elastic Inference
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.08741v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Most LLM architectures have fixed compute demands determined at training time. We propose a novel architecture that combines the Mixture-of-Experts architecture with shallow experts and a novel dynamic-depth system to make the extent of a forward pass dynamically adjustable. Our approach lets the model automatically determine the compute needed for a given task, paired with a system to scale it down after training without retraining when the execution environment demands faster or cheaper inference. ArXiv cs.AI.title: AttentionSwitch: Jailbreak Defense for LLMs via Joint Learning of Sparse Attention-Head Selection and Scaling
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.08752v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language models have achieved remarkable performance across a wide range of tasks, yet they remain susceptible to jailbreak attacks that circumvent safety mechanisms and elicit harmful or unintended outputs. Although safety can be improved through model fine-tuning, such approaches can be computationally expensive and may degrade previously acquired capabilities through catastrophic forgetting. Recent jailbreak defenses have therefore explored targeted interventions on specific model components associated with unsafe behavior. However, exi

ArXiv cs.AI.title: Debate to Deceive: Poisoning LLM's Fact-Checking via Game-Theoretic Multi-Agent Debate
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.08756v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Knowledge attacks on Large Language Models, such as manipulating fact-checking judgments, pose significant risks to AI reliability. Existing approaches -- adversarial suffix/template injection and single-agent self-reflection -- lack robustness across diverse defenses and are prone to confirmation bias and costly trial-and-error, respectively. ArXiv cs.AI.title: Jacobian-Causal Memory Control for Persistent Memory in Language Model Systems
ArXiv cs.AI.description:
arXiv:2611.08779v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Persistent-memory systems choose not only which records are retrieved but which prior information can alter current inference. We propose Jacobian-causal memory control (JCMC), which represents each authorized memory intervention by a predicted influence signature in a shared behavioral measurement space, selects interventions against a target effect and side-effect budget, and compares predicted with observed effects before retaining or rolling back the intervention. Under explicit smoothness and bounded-estimation assumptions, we prove a quadr

ArXiv cs.LG.title: FasterRW: An Efficient Prior-Assisted Random Walk Solver for Thermal Analysis
ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.08490v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Thermal simulation is becoming increasingly critical in modern IC design and manufacturing. Feynman--Kac random walk methods can estimate localized temperatures without solving the global field, but in practical settings without Dirichlet boundaries they require very long paths to control the truncation residual. This paper presents FasterRW, a continuation-value framework for accelerating Feynman--Kac thermal random walks. ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.08494v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Capturing sheet-metal localisation physics with a trained surrogate inside a finite element (FEM) solver requires the surrogate to deliver consistent predictions irrespective of the solver's strain-increment count, which is difficult to control in non-linear explicit codes. ArXiv cs.LG.title: Rethinking Data Selection as Distribution Matching on Semantic Manifolds
ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.08495v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Instruction tuning of large language models and large vision language models relies on massive training data, which incurs substantial computational and storage costs. Meanwhile, training data often contains redundancy, noise, and low quality samples. Existing data selection methods mostly rely on diversity, importance, or a combination of both, without explicitly constraining the distributional consistency between the selected subset and the full data in the embedding space. We propose QMAC, a quality aware multiband characteristic function mat

ArXiv cs.LG.title: Generative Reconstruction of Full-Field Sensor States for Safety-Critical Digital Twins
ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.08499v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Accurate reconstruction of incomplete sensor fields is critical for state awareness in safety-critical digital twins (DTs). Thermocouples in high-temperature and radiation environments may drift, fail, or become intermittently unavailable, causing partial observability. ArXiv cs.LG.title: Adaptive Depth Aggregation in Graph Transformers for Long-Range Graph Reasoning
ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.08500v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Graph Transformers improve long-range node-to-node communication through global or structure-aware interactions. However, improving cross-node communication does not determine how computations produced at different depths should be combined. Standard residual streams accumulate successive computations with fixed unit coefficients shared across nodes. ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.08502v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The remarkable generalization of modern over-parameterized neural networks defies classical statistical learning bounds. Here we establish that optimization trajectories in billion-parameter models do not sample the ambient dimension $\mathbb{R}^N$ homogeneously; instead, they are dynamically constrained to a low-dimensional execution submanifold $\mathcal{M}_{\text{exec}}$ (with empirically observed effective dimension $d_{\text{eff}} \le 12$). ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.08507v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) show strong zero-shot reasoning capabilities, yet their sensitivity to prompt context raises questions about reliability in deployment. This study investigates whether geographic context embedded in prompts influences LLM-based chronic kidney disease (CKD) screening, independent of any change in patient features. ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.08512v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: High-fidelity computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations of nuclear reactor systems are computationally expensive, motivating machine learning methods that reduce cost while preserving accuracy. Multifidelity surrogate modeling addresses this by combining inexpensive low-fidelity data with limited high-fidelity data. ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.08522v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Recent work reports large gains for LLM agents on low-budget molecular optimization. We measure the contributions of online optimization, retrievable task information, and permissive oracle landscapes. On PMO at 50 oracle calls, a GPT-4o mini agent's sum AUC falls from 14.44 to 4.85 after task names and curated reference compounds are hidden. ArXiv cs.LG.title: Evolutionary Adaptive Metric Learning: A Multi-Objective Framework for Learning Local Distance Functions in Nearest Neighbor Classification
ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.08549v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Nearest neighbour classifiers inherit the geometry of their distance function. Fixed distances and globally learned metrics apply the same geometry throughout the input space, although relevant feature directions may vary across regions. We propose EAML (Evolutionary Adaptive Metric Learning), a framework that learns instance-dependent positive-definite metrics through a low-dimensional parameterization. ArXiv cs.LG.title: How Small Can We Go? Calibrating Activation-Cache Compression for SAE Training
ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.08551v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: To train a sparse autoencoder (SAE), you need a massive cache of model activations. We look into the effects that compression has on an SAE in two ways: we keep the original fp32-trained SAE and pass the compressed cache into the same SAE to see how many feature activations stay the same (the frozen-SAE test), and we retrain an SAE on the compressed cache and see how many of the original features still exist (the retraining test). ArXiv cs.LG.title: Minimum-Sufficient Knowledge and Computation for Wind Energy Predictive Analysis
ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.08558v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Resource-constrained cyber-physical decision systems often apply fixed sensing, knowledge, and computational pipelines despite state-dependent information needs. We introduce Minimum-Sufficient Knowledge and Computation (MSKC), a resource-aware computing principle: select the least-costly route meeting decision-risk and deployment constraints, escalating only when cheaper routes are insufficient. ArXiv cs.LG.title: PINNeval: A Comprehensive Evaluation Standard for Physics-Informed Neural Networks
ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.08559v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN) literature has produced a rapidly expanding catalogue of methods. We divide a PINN training pipeline systematically into four components and observe that many existing benchmarks study these components in isolation. These components are domain-importance adaptation, loss balancing, neural network architecture, and optimization scheme. ArXiv cs.LG.title: Not All Misalignment Is Alike: A Decomposed Benchmark for Emergent Misalignment
ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.08569v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Emergent misalignment (EM), in which fine-tuning on a narrow task induces misaligned behaviour on unrelated prompts, has been demonstrated across a wide range of datasets, model families, and training setups. Yet, most studies continue to rely on the evaluation approach introduced in the original EM paper, producing rates that are sensitive to the small set of evaluation questions used, the choice of judge, and the thresholds applied. ArXiv cs.LG.description:
arXiv:2611.08634v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Machine learning (ML) and generative AI have recently made impressive progress in understanding physics. We explore a hierarchy of prediction problems stemming from chaotic three-body systems and benchmark existing ML approaches, including general-purpose prediction algorithms and those that build on top of foundational physics models.
